name: AnchorTest.Planted.cert_01
witness_note: n = 6 satisfies both; n = 3 breaks 2 ∣ n and n = 2 breaks 3 ∣ n, and neither is divisible by 6.

name: AnchorTest.Planted.cert_02
witness_note: a = 1, b = c = 0 satisfies both; a = 2 with (b, c) = (1, 0) or (0, 1) breaks one divisibility and the conclusion.

name: AnchorTest.Planted.cert_03
witness_note: x = 3/2 satisfies both; x = 0 breaks the lower bound and x = 2 breaks the upper bound, each failing the conclusion.

name: AnchorTest.Planted.cert_04
witness_note: x = y = 0 satisfies all three; (x, y) = (-1, 1), (1, -1) and (0, 1) each break one hypothesis and give x ≠ y.

name: AnchorTest.Planted.cert_05
witness_note: s = t = ∅ satisfies both; s = {0}, t = {1} breaks the subset hypothesis and s = ∅, t = {0} breaks the cardinality hypothesis.

name: AnchorTest.Planted.cert_06
witness_note: [1] satisfies both; [0] breaks positivity and [] breaks nonemptiness, both with sum 0.

name: AnchorTest.Planted.cert_07
witness_note: f = id, a = 0, b = 1 satisfies both; f x = -x with a = 1, b = 0 breaks strict monotonicity; f = id with a = b = 0 breaks f a < f b.

name: AnchorTest.Planted.cert_08
witness_note: Needs a nonabelian group: in the permutations of Fin 3, swap 0 1 and swap 1 2 break commutativity; a 3-cycle paired with 1 breaks either square hypothesis.

name: AnchorTest.Planted.cert_09
witness_note: Concrete monoid ℕ under multiplication: a = b = c = 1 satisfies both; (a, b, c) = (1, 2, 1) and (1, 1, 2) each break one hypothesis.

name: AnchorTest.Planted.cert_10
witness_note: A constant function satisfies both; f x = -x is antitone but not monotone, id is monotone but not antitone, and both have f 0 ≠ f 1.

name: AnchorTest.Planted.vac_01
witness_note: a < b and b ≤ a give a < a.

name: AnchorTest.Planted.vac_02
witness_note: n and n + 1 cannot both be even.

name: AnchorTest.Planted.vac_03
witness_note: x^2 + y^2 - 2xy = (x - y)^2 is never negative.

name: AnchorTest.Planted.vac_04
witness_note: 6 ∣ a makes a even, so a + 1 is odd and not divisible by 4.

name: AnchorTest.Planted.vac_05
witness_note: A subset of range 3 has at most 3 elements.

name: AnchorTest.Planted.vac_06
witness_note: sin^2 θ + cos^2 θ = 1 for every real θ, a lemma not visible in the statement.

name: AnchorTest.Planted.vac_07
witness_note: No prime divides 1.

name: AnchorTest.Planted.vac_08
witness_note: a < b < c < a is a cycle of strict inequalities; no two of the three conflict alone.

name: AnchorTest.Planted.vac_09
witness_note: Increasing at every step forces f 2 < f 5 (needs strict monotonicity from the step condition).

name: AnchorTest.Planted.vac_10
witness_note: Two entries each at most 2 sum to at most 4, not 5.

name: AnchorTest.Planted.dec_01
witness_note: b ≠ 0 is removable because a / 0 = 0 ≠ 1 in a field; ℚ with a = 0, b = 1 shows a / b = 1 is load-bearing.

name: AnchorTest.Planted.dec_02
witness_note: 0 < n is implied by 2 ≤ n; n = 1 shows 2 ≤ n is load-bearing.

name: AnchorTest.Planted.dec_03
witness_note: 0 < x is removable because 2 is the only real cube root of 8 (the proof uses it anyway); x = 1 shows the cube hypothesis is load-bearing.

name: AnchorTest.Planted.dec_04
witness_note: s.Nonempty is removable since card is monotone under subset; s = {0, 1}, t = {0} shows s ⊆ t is load-bearing.

name: AnchorTest.Planted.dec_05
witness_note: l ≠ [] is implied by a ∈ l; l = [1], a = 0 shows membership is load-bearing.

name: AnchorTest.Planted.dec_06
witness_note: a ≠ 0 is implied by a ∣ b with 0 < b; (a, b) = (2, 1) and (2, 0) show the other two are load-bearing.

name: AnchorTest.Planted.dec_07
witness_note: Continuity is removable since strict monotonicity alone gives injectivity; a constant function with a = 0, b = 1 and id with a = 0, b = 1 show the others are load-bearing.

name: AnchorTest.Planted.dec_08
witness_note: Commutativity is removable since a * b = 1 implies b * a = 1 in any group (the proof uses it anyway); swap 0 1 with b = 1 in the permutations of Fin 3 shows a * b = 1 is load-bearing.

name: AnchorTest.Planted.dec_09
witness_note: a ≠ c is implied by a < b ≤ c; in ℕ, (a, b, c) = (1, 0, 0) and (1, 2, 0) show the other two are load-bearing.

name: AnchorTest.Planted.dec_10
witness_note: x ≠ y is implied by x < y; (x, y) = (-2, -1) and (2, 1) show the other two are load-bearing.

name: AnchorTest.Planted.nohyp_1
witness_note: Only variables a b : ℕ.

name: AnchorTest.Planted.nohyp_2
witness_note: A type, a Group instance and two elements; no proposition binders.

name: AnchorTest.Planted.nohyp_3
witness_note: The conclusion is a negation, which is a conclusion and not a binder.

name: AnchorTest.Planted.nohyp_4
witness_note: Only a list variable.

name: AnchorTest.Planted.nohyp_5
witness_note: The conclusion is a ≠, which is a conclusion and not a binder.

name: AnchorTest.Planted.depd_1
witness_note: The conclusion builds an element of Fin n from the proof of 0 < n.

name: AnchorTest.Planted.depd_2
witness_note: The conclusion uses the proof of l ≠ [] as the argument of List.head.

name: AnchorTest.Planted.depd_3
witness_note: The second hypothesis's type mentions the proof of l ≠ [] through List.head.

name: AnchorTest.Planted.depd_4
witness_note: The conclusion passes the nonemptiness proof to Finset.min' and Finset.max'.

name: AnchorTest.Planted.depd_5
witness_note: A model binder v follows the hypothesis 0 < n; the later hypothesis and the conclusion both build an element of Fin n from its proof.
